blocks.prompt: 11. Find the general solution of the differential equation \((e^{2x} + e^{-2x})\,dy + (e^{-2x} - e^{2x})\,dx = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Only \(x\) appears in the coefficients, so the equation is separable: \(dy = f(x)\,dx\).
Plan: make \(dy\) the subject; the numerator turns out to be half the derivative of the denominator, so the integral is a logarithm.
steps:
Given: \((e^{2x} + e^{-2x})\,dy + (e^{-2x} - e^{2x})\,dx = 0\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: separable; write \(dy = f(x)\,dx\) and integrate using \(\int\frac{f'}{f} = \ln|f|\).

Separate
\[dy = \dfrac{e^{2x} - e^{-2x}}{e^{2x} + e^{-2x}}\,dx\]
Why: move the \(dx\) term across (its bracket changes sign: \(-(e^{-2x} - e^{2x}) = e^{2x} - e^{-2x}\)) and divide by \(e^{2x} + e^{-2x}\).

Look at the derivative of the denominator
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{2x} + e^{-2x}) = 2e^{2x} - 2e^{-2x}\]
\[= 2(e^{2x} - e^{-2x})\]
Why: chain rule, \(\frac{d}{dx}e^{kx} = ke^{kx}\). So the numerator is half of this derivative.

Integrate
\[y = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(e^{2x} + e^{-2x}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|C|\]
Why: \(\int\frac{f'}{f} = \ln|f|\), times \(\frac{1}{2}\). The constant is written as \(\frac{1}{2}\ln|C|\) so that the logs combine.

Simplify
\[2y = \ln|C(e^{2x} + e^{-2x})|\]
Why: multiply by 2 and use \(\ln a + \ln b = \ln ab\).

Check
From \(y = \frac{1}{2}\ln(e^{2x} + e^{-2x}) + \text{const}\):
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2e^{2x} - 2e^{-2x}}{e^{2x} + e^{-2x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{e^{2x} - e^{-2x}}{e^{2x} + e^{-2x}}\]
This is the separated equation.
